dct_description_sm: Latitudinal gradients in species richness, with decreasing diversity at high latitudes, is one of the most recognized patterns of species distribution. However, it remains unclear if these patterns of distribution hold for microorganisms. Latitudinal gradients have been observed in marine bacteria. In contrast, there appears to be contradictory evidence for latitudinal gradients in soil microbial communities.  Studies have found latitudinal gradients, no gradients, or even increased diversity at higher latitudes. In this project, we present the first in-depth characterization of bacteria inhabiting biological soil crusts (biocrusts) on high Arctic polar desert soils at the northernmost terrestrial system in the Arctic, in order to compare the diversity of these systems to bacterial populations from more temperate latitudes.
dct_title_s: Bacterial diversity in permafrost water tracks, Ward Hunt Island
